problem:
The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=1,$ ${x}_{2}=-3,$ and ${x}_{3}=4,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $5.$ Find $P(x).$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}${x}^{3}\,-$
{{field-2}}${x}^{2}\,-$
{{field-3}}$x\,+$
{{field-4}}
worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=1,$ ${x}_{2}=-3,$ and ${x}_{3}=4,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=5,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =5(x-1)(x-(-3))(x-4) \\  & =5(x-1)(x+3)(x-4)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5(x-1)(x+3)(x-4) & =5({x}^{2}+2x-3)(x-4) \\  & =5({x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}-8x-3x+12) \\  & =5({x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-11x+12) \\  & =5{x}^{3}-10{x}^{2}-55x+60.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=5{x}^{3}-10{x}^{2}-55x+60.$
